sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Swadeshi Movement** (1905) and **Civil Disobedience Movement** (1930) led by **Mahatma Gandhi** and nationalist leaders.
**Swadeshi Movement:** **1905** (Partition of Bengal); **Civil Disobedience Movement:** **1930** (Dandi March to Gandhi-Irwin Pact).
**Swadeshi Movement:** Centered in **Bengal** and spread nationwide; **Civil Disobedience Movement:** Pan-India, starting from **Sabarmati Ashram** to **Dandi**.
**Mahatma Gandhi**, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Bipin Chandra Pal**, **Subhash Chandra Bose**, **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**.
Marked a major shift from moderate petitions to mass mobilization, economic self-reliance (**Swadeshi**), and direct challenge to British authority.
Boycott of foreign goods, promotion of **Khadi**, **Salt Satyagraha**, refusal to pay taxes, and participation of women and youth.
High-scoring static GK area covering exact dates, Viceroy names, session locations, and key slogans frequently asked in UP exams.
Introduction of **Charkha** as a national symbol, **Round Table Conferences**, and the historic **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** of **1931**.

items.title: 1. Background of Swadeshi Movement (1905)
items.content:
• **Lord Curzon** announced the **Partition of Bengal** on **July 20, 1905** to curb nationalist upsurge.
• Formal proclamation of Swadeshi on **October 7, 1905** at **Town Hall, Calcutta**.
• Partition took effect on **October 16, 1905**, observed as a day of **mourning** and **Raksha Bandhan**.
• **Mnemonic for Extremist Leaders (Lal-Bal-Pal):** **LLB** -> **L**ala Lajpat Rai, **L**okmanya Tilak, **B**ipin Chandra Pal.

items.title: 2. Methods and Spread of Swadeshi
items.content:
• Boycott of **British goods**, schools, colleges, and law courts.
• Promotion of **indigenous (Swadeshi)** industries, handlooms, national banks, and insurance companies.
• Establishment of **National Council of Education** in **1906**.
• **Viceroy during Partition:** **Lord Curzon** (1899–1905).
• **President of 1905 Benaras Session:** **Gopal Krishan Gokhale**.

items.title: 3. Transition to Gandhian Era & Non-Cooperation (1920)
items.content:
• Return of **Mahatma Gandhi** from South Africa in **January 1915** (**Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**).
• Early experiments with Satyagraha: **Champaran** (1917), **Ahmedabad Mill Strike** (1918), **Kheda** (1918).
• Launch of **Non-Cooperation Movement** in **1920** (abruptly suspended after **Chauri Chaura incident** on **February 4, 1922**).

items.title: 4. Civil Disobedience Movement & Salt Satyagraha (1930)
items.content:
• **Lahore Session (December 1929):** Presided over by **Jawaharlal Nehru**; passed **Purna Swaraj** resolution.
• **Dandi March:** Started on **March 12, 1930** with **78 trusted volunteers** from **Sabarmati Ashram**.
• Reached Dandi on **April 6, 1930** (distance of **240 miles** or **385 km**) and broke the salt law.
• **Mnemonic for Dandi March details:** **78** followers, **24** days, **240** miles -> **78-24-240**.

items.title: 5. Spread of Civil Disobedience Across India
items.content:
• **Tamil Nadu:** **C. Rajagopalachari** led march from Trichy to Vedaranyam.
• **Malabar:** **K. Kelappan** led salt march from Calicut to Payyanur.
• **North-West Frontier Province:** **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** (Badshah Khan) founded **Khudai Khidmatgars** (Red Shirts).
• **Nagaland/Manipur:** **Gaidinliu** (Zeliangrong movement) raised the banner of revolt at age **13**.

items.title: 6. Gandhi-Irwin Pact and Round Table Conferences
items.content:
• **First Round Table Conference (1930):** Boycotted by Congress.
• **Gandhi-Irwin Pact (Delhi Pact):** Signed on **March 5, 1931**; Congress agreed to suspend Civil Disobedience and attend RTC.
• **Second Round Table Conference (1931):** Mahatma Gandhi attended as sole Congress representative via **S.S. Rajputana** ship.
• **Communal Award (1932):** Announced by **Ramsay MacDonald**, leading to **Poona Pact** between Gandhi and **B.R. Ambedkar** on **September 24, 1932**.

items.definition: Use the acronym **C-N-C** -> **C**hamparan (1917) -> **N**on-Cooperation (1920) -> **C**ivil Disobedience (1930).

items.term: Trick 2: Three Round Table Conferences Years
items.definition: Consecutive years starting from 1930 -> **30, 31, 32** (Remember: **1930, 1931, 1932**).
**78** men walked **24** days covering **240** miles -> Remember **78-24-240**.
**Lal**a Lajpat Rai (Punjab), **Bal** Gangadhar Tilak (Bombay/Maharashtra), **Bpi**n Chandra Pal (Bengal).
Use **CAK** -> **C**hamparan (1917), **A**hmedabad (1918), **K**heda (1918).
Swadeshi = **Curzon** (1905), Non-Cooperation = **Chelmsford** (1920), Civil Disobedience = **Irwin** (1930).

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Surat Split year with Swadeshi launch
items.definition: Swadeshi movement started in **1905**, but the formal **Surat Split** between Moderates and Extremists happened in **1907**.

items.term: Mistake 2: Gandhi attending all Round Table Conferences
items.definition: Gandhi attended **only the Second** Round Table Conference (1931) under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. **B.R. Ambedkar** attended all three.

items.term: Mistake 3: Purna Swaraj session location and President
items.definition: The historic 1929 Purna Swaraj resolution was passed at **Lahore**, not Calcutta, under the presidency of **Jawaharlal Nehru**, not Motilal Nehru.

items.term: Mistake 4: Dandi March duration and distance
items.definition: Students confuse days and miles. It took **24 days** to cover **240 miles** (385 km) with **78 followers**.
Poona Pact was signed between **B.R. Ambedkar** and **Madan Mohan Malaviya** (on behalf of Gandhi, who was fasting in Yerwada Jail).

items.term: Mistake 6: Launch date of Civil Disobedience vs Dandi March
items.definition: Dandi March started on **March 12, 1930**, but the formal Civil Disobedience Movement officially began when the salt law was broken on **April 6, 1930**.
Announced by **Lord Curzon** in **1905**; sparked the **Swadeshi and Boycott** movement across India.
Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal (**Lal-Bal-Pal**) championed radical nationalist methods.
INC split into Moderates and Extremists in **1907** at the Surat session presided over by **Rash Behari Ghosh**.
Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on **January 9, 1915**.
Gandhi's first civil disobedience in India in **1917** against the **Tinkathia system** in Bihar.
Launched in **1920**; suspended in **1922** due to the **Chauri Chaura violence** in Gorakhpur, UP.
Passed at the **Lahore Session (1929)** under **Jawaharlal Nehru**, declaring complete independence as the goal.
Commenced on **March 12, 1930**, from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to break the salt law.
Saw widespread participation across India including **Khudai Khidmatgars** in NWFP and salt marches in Madras and Malabar.
Signed on **March 5, 1931**, leading to the suspension of Civil Disobedience and Gandhi's participation in the **Second RTC**.
British introduced separate electorates in **1932**; nullified by the **Poona Pact** between Ambedkar and Gandhi.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks exact dates and matching pairs (e.g., matching movements with years or leaders). Memorize the chronology from 1905 (Bengal Partition) to 1932 (Poona Pact) sequentially.
Pay special attention to UP-centric facts such as the Chauri Chaura incident (Gorakhpur, 1922) and Mahatma Gandhi's early movements like Champaran (Bihar).
Questions often trick students regarding Gandhi's presence at the Round Table Conferences. Remember he attended ONLY the Second RTC (1931), while B.R. Ambedkar attended all three.
Do not confuse the Lahore Session President. Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the 1929 Purna Swaraj session, whereas Motilal Nehru presided over the 1919 Amritsar session.

keyTakeaways: Swadeshi Movement (1905) marked the birth of economic nationalism and boycott of British goods.
Mahatma Gandhi transformed the freedom struggle into a mass movement through Satyagraha and Ahimsa.
Dandi March (1930) with 78 volunteers over 24 days triggered the nationwide Civil Disobedience Movement.
Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) brought the Congress to the negotiating table at the Second Round Table Conference in London.
Poona Pact (1932) resolved the controversy over separate electorates for Dalits without breaking Hindu unity.
